subject: SIG request: connectivity evidence pack + VPC configuration snapshots
messages:
From: Jenna Smith <j.smith@acmecorp.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: security-eng@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-11-15 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG follow-up: network evidence we still need

Hi Rohan—

Thanks again for the walk-through earlier today. As we kick off the SIG review, the security team asked me to collect concrete network evidence for the routing and TAP items. Specifically they requested:

- VPC topology snapshot(s) showing subnet allocations and route tables (latest configuration as of today)
- Egress IP ranges used by the hosted inference endpoints
- Any private endpoint / PrivateLink configuration snippets and ARN/endpoint IDs
- Recent VPC Flow Logs sample (1 hour) and guidance on retention windows
- Completed peering request form / evidence of peering approvals

Can you share a packaged evidence bundle for those items? Ideally we get this by EOD next Tuesday (2026-11-23) to stay on schedule. Also please point us to any traceroute or connectivity test you can provide that demonstrates egress path consistency.

Appreciate it—if a particular artifact needs to come from another teammate, loop them in.

Best,
Jenna
Jenna Smith
Security Program Manager, Acme Corp

--
Acme Security Team
security-eng@acmecorp.com
From: rohan_mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Smith <j.smith@acmecorp.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-15 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: network evidence we still need

Hi Jenna—

Thanks for the clear list. We can assemble everything you asked for. Quick clarifications so we deliver exactly what you need:

1) VPC snapshots: do you want exported CloudFormation/Terraform state or PNG export of the topology? We can provide both; PNG snapshots are faster.
2) Egress IP ranges: do you need the full historical range for the last 30 days or the canonical published egress set we advertise for allowlisting?
3) Flow logs: we'll provide a 1-hour sample in gzipped JSON and a summary of our retention policy (we retain 90 days for flow logs in hosted tenancy).
4) Private endpoints: we'll include the PrivateLink configuration snippet and the endpoint IDs for the current production variant.

Tentative plan: Hannah will produce topology + peering forms, Vivek will run egress/flow log exports, Kimberly will validate the PrivateLink config and retention statements. I'll collate into a single zip and upload to the Drive link and send back a checklist.

We aim to have the package ready by EOD Monday (2026-11-22) — earlier than your requested date — unless you prefer Tuesday.

Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rohan_mehta@redwood.com
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: j.smith@acmecorp.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-16 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: network evidence we still need

Hi team / Jenna—

Attaching: peering-request-form.pdf and a PNG export of the current VPC topology (vpc_diagram_v2.png). Notes:

- We use dedicated VPCs per-customer for customer-dedicated deployments; the hosted API runs in our shared tenancy with per-tenant isolation at the application layer. The attached PNG highlights the production inference VPC and the route table used for public egress.
- For peering: we support VPC Peering for Dedicated customers and PrivateLink for hosted integrations. The peering form includes the expected CIDR ranges and the minimal route updates the customer needs to add.
- Routes: the production egress goes through a set of NAT instances behind a NAT autoscaling group; there's no direct internet gateway on the inference subnets.

I'll also include a short annotated screenshot of the route table entries in the Drive folder.

-h
Hannah Schmitt
Network Security Lead, Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, j.smith@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-11-17 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: network evidence we still need

Jenna / team—

Uploading the canonical egress list (egress_ip_ranges.csv) to the Drive link and including a short readme:

- Canonical egress set is what we publish for IP allowlisting; it covers all hosted inference endpoints across the us-west and us-east regions. We publish updates as part of our release notes and notify customers with a 7-day window for changes.
- For the specific tenant you are evaluating under ACME-2026, there is an additional NAT egress IP (10.200.45.10 NAT EIP mapped to 54.213.120.44) — I included that in the CSV and marked it with the tenant column.
- We captured a 1-hour VPC Flow Logs sample (flowlogs_sample_20261117.gz) and a short summary of observed connections in the same folder. That sample shows the consistent egress through the NAT EIP referenced above.

Additional notes on topology: if you're using VPC peering, ensure your route tables do not advertise overlapping CIDRs. For customers requiring a private connection we recommend PrivateLink; the privatelink-config-snippet.txt contains the API payload we use to create the endpoint services.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jenna Smith <j.smith@acmecorp.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: security-eng@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-11-18 07:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: network evidence we still need

Thanks — this looks good. Two quick follow-ups from our infra team after reviewing the artifacts:

1) Can you provide a short traceroute (three repeated runs) from an inference endpoint to our collector endpoint (ingest.acme-logs.com) so we can confirm egress path consistency and minimal hops? If you can include timestamps and the originating instance id that will help.
2) For PrivateLink: please confirm whether the endpoint service uses an NLB with static IPs or if it relies on regional AWS mappings (we're specifically trying to confirm that there are stable endpoints we can sign to the allowlist).

If you can drop the traceroute output and a one-line confirmation about the PrivateLink fronting (NLB vs AWS-managed) that would close the last of our questions.

Jenna
From: rohan_mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: j.smith@acmecorp.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-20 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: network evidence we still need

Jenna—

Attached is the compiled evidence pack (see Drive folder). Quick answers inline: 

- Traceroute: we executed three runs from a production inference instance (instance-id i-0a12b3c4d5e6f7g8) to your collector host (ingest.acme-logs.com) on 2026-11-20 between 15:20–15:26 PST. The outputs are included as traceroutes_acme_20261120.txt and show consistent egress via NAT EIP 54.213.120.44 with stable intermediate hops (avg 6 hops).

- PrivateLink fronting: the endpoint service for hosted PrivateLink customers is fronted by an NLB we control; the NLB has stable assigned static IPs per region when created. The privatelink-config-snippet.txt includes the endpoint-service ID and the NLB ARN. For Dedicated deployments using VPC Peering there is no NLB on our side — peering relies on route table updates only.

Next steps: I've uploaded sig_evidence_index.xlsx which maps each SIG question to the artifact filename and a short rationale. Please review and let us know if anything else is required. If this closes your list we can mark the SIG question set as answered and move to the attestation follow-up.

Thanks,
Rohan
